content.title: About
content.content: Sausage and vegetables is a dish that pairs juicy boiled or fried sausage with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale, Swiss chard). It is prepared without potatoes and without a tomato‑based sauce, making it suitable for low‑starch and low‑acid diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and compounds that support detoxification.
Carrots contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens are excellent sources of iron and folate.
Lean sausage provides a quick source of complete protein.
The dish can be adapted to many cuisines by changing spices and the sausage preparation method.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Sausage supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, potassium and magnesium, which benefit immunity and heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Beta‑carotene and phytochemicals in broccoli help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from carrots and leafy greens promotes healthy bowel movement.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Absence of potatoes and tomato sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages can be high in salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium varieties.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Some sausages contain saturated fat, which in excess may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A minority of individuals may be allergic or intolerant to certain types of meat.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: Leafy greens can contain oxalates; those prone to kidney stones should consume them in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté sliced sausage until golden, then add carrots, broccoli and leafy greens, cooking 5‑7 minutes until vegetables are tender. Season with garlic, paprika and fresh herbs if desired. Serve hot as a main dish or with whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When reheating, add a splash of water to keep vegetables from drying out. Do not leave sausage at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
